Subject: High P99 latency since 07:45 PDT - Greengrid prod

We're seeing a major P99 jump on our production tenant starting ~07:45 PDT. API calls that normally return in <250ms are spiking to 1.4-2.0s and a subset of requests are timing out. Traffic profile hasn't changed on our side. This started right before our morning batch.

Subject: Re: High P99 latency since 07:45 PDT - Greengrid prod

Quick update from SRE triage:
- No control plane rollout noted between 07:00–08:00. No infra autoscaler events in us-west.
- We see a sudden drop in prefix cache hit rate for this tenant at 07:46 (cache_hit_rate 92% -> 38%). A correlated spike in backend model GPU queues starting at 07:47.
- Early hypothesis: an upstream change in request prefix variety (new prompts/batch patterns) caused cache churn and increased KV cache misses, pushing latency into tail.

Immediate mitigation options (short-lived, can be executed in ~10m):
1) Route Greengrid traffic to a higher-priority capacity pool (short routing override) — will reduce queuing but has slight cost impact.
2) Apply temporary per-tenant KV cache warmup by replaying recent prefixes to fill cache (we can run a targeted warmup job).
3) Throttle non-critical long-running requests via route-based limits.

I recommend action 1 + 2 in parallel. I'm attaching an automated snapshot of p99 and current queue length and a one-page run of the routing override steps. If you approve, I'll execute the routing override and kick off warmup.

Attachments: p99_snapshot_20270520.csv, routing_override_steps.txt

Karthik Iyer
SRE Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks Karthik — that matches what eng is seeing from model-side metrics. Quick notes and a product ask:
- Root cause assessment so far points to cache eviction churn exacerbated by a recent increase in prompt diversity for a small set of customers. The longer-term fix is to add a per-tenant sticky prefix cache and smarter eviction policy (we've prototyped this but it's not on the mainline).
- Short-term: I support Karthik's routing override + warmup. We should also add a transient config to preferentially route Greengrid to an instance class with a larger KV cache (modest infra change, low risk).

Product/roadmap ask (decision needed if we want to avoid recurring incidents):
1) Prioritize per-tenant sticky cache in Q3 roadmap (estimated 4–6 sprint effort across runtime + infra).
2) Add a tenant-level telemetry alert for cache-hit-rate dips below 60% (small prod signal + alerting work).

If Leadership/Product (Jonas) can greenlight elevated priority for the sticky cache item, we can schedule a soft-target for the Q3 sprint kickoff. If not, we'll scope a narrower mitigation that buys more time (config route + telemetry).

Marissa Cole
Director, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: High P99 latency since 07:45 PDT - Greengrid prod

Hi Aditi — quick customer-facing update and ETA.

What happened (short): We observed a sudden increase in distinct request prefixes for your tenant at ~07:46 PDT which caused higher-than-normal cache churn on our end. That increased backend queuing and raised P99 latency.

What we did (right now):
- Shifted Greengrid traffic to a higher-priority capacity pool to clear queued requests (routing override executed at 08:48).
- Ran a targeted KV-cache warmup to restore hot prefixes for your tenant.
- Applied a transient tenant config to prefer instances with larger KV caches.

Impact now: P99 has dropped from ~1.8s to ~260ms for the requests we sampled. We're continuing to monitor across all routes and will keep you updated.

Next steps and timeline:
- We're observing for 60 minutes; if stable we'll remove the routing override and keep the transient config in place.
- Engineering has proposed a roadmap change (per-tenant sticky cache + hit-rate alerting) to prevent recurrence. We'll share a proposal and target timeline by EOW.

ETA for final postmortem: 48 hours.

If there's a specific merchant flow you want us to prioritize validating, flag the request id prefixes and we'll run targeted checks.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll follow up with a status at 11:30 PDT.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
